diagnoses.description: Date disambiguation failure: invoice contains multiple date-like strings; the pipeline likely selected a secondary header-adjacent date/time token (or OCR-corrupted label line) instead of the primary header “Date:” field.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 034.jpg date_correct=false while amount_correct=true. The image shows a clear header block with “Date: 09/03/2018” near receipt metadata, but the historical prediction is 2018-08-09, consistent with selecting a different dd/mm token elsewhere (or an OCR-mutated DATE→DATA line noted in prior history). This is a classic multi-candidate selection problem requiring label-tolerant matching + header-block preference.

diagnoses.description: Total selection failure due to OCR digit-flip outlier and competing total-like lines (incl/excl GST, rounded total, payment). The pipeline selected an implausible outlier (702.00) instead of the internally consistent payable total.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 074.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount="702.00". Visual inspection of 074.jpg shows multiple anchors around 102.00 (Subtotal, Total incl. of GST, Total Amt Rounded, Payment), while 702.00 is a typical OCR 1→7 digit flip. This indicates selection logic over-trusted a single corrupted line/variant and lacked a strict anchor-consistency override.

diagnoses.description: Rounding precedence failure: receipt shows an inclusive total, a rounding adjustment, then a final payable TOTAL; the pipeline selected the pre-rounding value (23.26) instead of the final total after rounding (23.25).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 077.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount="23.26". The image clearly shows “Rounding Adj: -0.01” followed by a bold “TOTAL: 23.25”, while an earlier line shows “Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26”. Exact-match scoring requires a hard rule: final total after rounding wins.

diagnoses.description: Schema/normalization failure: total_amount was emitted as an empty string instead of null; additionally, this receipt layout includes an “Amount” column header that can trigger split-line fallback to an item amount unless explicitly excluded, and OCR may corrupt the decimal separator (e.g., 92:80) and the GRAND TOTAL keyword (e.g., GrandTota./GrandTotal.).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 078.jpg amount_correct=false; prediction total_amount="" violates task requirement (must be null on failure). Visual inspection of 078.jpg shows a table header “Description Qty Price Amount” plus summary lines “Total: 92.80” and “Grand Total: 92.80” and payment lines “Cash Received: 100.00”, “Change: 7.20”. Prior history indicates OCR variants like “a Total — 92:80” and “GrandTota.”, which require decimal-separator normalization and tolerant keyword matching; regardless, empty string must be converted to null.
